# BOOK 1: Adele Doring of the Sunnyside Club (Grace May North, 1919; Gutenberg 62151)

## Cast
- **Adele Doring**: club president, 13 at start (turns 13 on Eva's party day), nut-brown/golden-brown braids and curls, rose-colored sweater-coat, broad-brimmed hat. Calls father "Giant Father/Giant Daddy/Daddy" (he calls her "Heart's Desire"), mother "Adorable Mother/mumsie." Writes verses.
- **Jack Doring**: Adele's brother, a year older, indolent, later "Pirate the Terrible," chief of the Jolly Pirates (7 boys).
- **Kate**: Irish cook, calls Adele "Colleen."
- **Terrence**: Mr. Doring's handyman. **Firefly**: Adele's black pony, red cart; whistle brings him; loves sugar lumps.
- **Sunny Seven** (Adele's club): 
  - **Rosamond "Rosie" Wright**: romantic, short golden curls, tatting, dislikes scrubbing.
  - **Doris Drexel**: father is bank president; grandmother's pillow; teases.
  - **Bertha Angel**: treasurer, practical, 13, tall, father a grocer; brother **Bob Angel** (teaser, drives hay-rack horses Jerry and Jingo, "Rastus" in disguise).
  - **Betty Burd** ("Burdie," "Bettykins," "Little One"): youngest, 11 (turns 12), petite, dark, sparkling; widowed mother, Mrs. Burd; uncle **George Wainwright**, young newspaper editor, calls her "Betsy Bobbets"/"Puss." Later pony **Star** (white forehead spot).
  - **Peggy Pierce**: father owns the Bee Hive department store; darling of father's heart; mischievous.
  - **Gertrude Willis** ("Trudie"): secretary, minister's daughter (father Rev. Willis), dearest friend of Adele, a writer, delicate in winter.
- **Miss Donovan**: Seven B teacher. **Mr. Dickerson**: principal.
- **Granny Dorset** (Sarie Dorset): ill, bedridden; violets; turns 70; wish: purple silk dress with lace neck and sleeves.
- **Mrs. Friend**: orphanage matron (Home is a mile out on the Lake Road).
- **Eva Dearman**: orphan, 13, golden-brown hair, blue eyes; father a wealthy broker who lost money; mother died; deed to worthless Arizona desert land; **Uncle Dick (Richard Dearman)**, "Cattle King of Silver Creek," Bar-X Ranch.
- **Amanda Brown**: surly orphan, black braids, later sings; mother a concert singer who begged her not to sing in concert halls. Married cowboy "Rusty Pete," had a baby.
- **Madge Peterson**: artist, ~18 (city, Dorchester); brother **Everett Peterson** (sailor, white flannels, capsized boat); car "Pigmy"; little brother Roberty-Bob (hunchback).
- **Eric Brownley** ("Kid," "Petey" is Everett's nickname): raised by **Jock Henderson** ("Daddy Jock"), a lumberman; **Little Bear** the bear (died of poison); **Fiddler Fritz**; **Pat Mahoney**. Eric is Sunnyside/Dorchester high-school pitcher.
- **Ching Ling**: Little Bear Inn cook.
- **Mrs. Melissa Green** (Mrs. Cyrus Green), **Susetta "Susie" Green** (daughter), **Mr. Cyrus Green** (ex-tavern keeper, Restwell estate on Lake Road).
- **Sally Grackle** (Miss Grackle): lives in gray house by pines north of village; sister **Miranda** eloped to Arizona with adventurer.
- **Quigleys** (Mr. Dan and Mrs. Betsy Quigley): cabin burned, sent to poorhouse; get cottage.
- **Grandpa 'Lijah Dally**: old neighbor, wolf story, miser story.
- **Mr. Drakely**: postman. **Uncle Danny**: deaf station-master (book 2 too).

## Chapters
1. **The Sunnyside Club**: April, Buttercup Meadows by stone wall. Club formed; Adele president (unanimous), Bertha treasurer, Gertrude secretary. Pledge: "We promise to look on the Sunnyside / And be kind and cheerful each day..." Meet under elm-tree.
2. **Secret Sanctum**: Town Sunnyside in valley; Little Bear Lake beyond hills; Lookout Hill; old sheep-herders' log cabin in Buttercup Meadows (maple wood, laughing brook). Father grants it. Rusty key, padlock; key hidden under log.
3. **Jolly Scrubbing-Party**: Saturday; Kate; Jack eats chocolate cupcake; robin song "Cheerily! Cheerily!"; Bertha director; scouring-powder; Betty lifts hot pail with broom; furniture scrubbed at brook; olives; Bertha's cream sugar cookie; plans: mosquito netting (item one), mattress, pine pillow, blue bowl with chip (item five), china-closet from orange boxes, bank, housewarming party.
4. **Adele's Secret**: Bob and Jack cart furniture. Adele late (dug violets for Granny Dorset). Betty answers "It's a secret!" to "capital of England." Adele's birthday next week; tells of Eva Dearman, orphan crying in empty classroom; plans surprise party for Eva. Meet Saturday at three.
5. **Pleasant Plans**: Eva's family history; Amanda Brown "disagreeable"; bank missing (Peggy had taken it to father's safe, forgotten). $6.33 in treasury. Mr. Pierce gives 12 locket necklaces in pink-silk-lined boxes at cost.
6. **Surprise Party**: Eva's 13th birthday; Eva dusts for Amanda ("Seeing _is_ believing!"); Jenny Dixon whispered insult; Amanda hides in linen closet; Eva refuses to go unless Amanda goes. Hay-rack with daisy garlands; Bob and Jack disguised as black waiters ("Rastus"); 13 pink candy roses on cake; "two noses" joke; "Garçon!"; lockets distributed; Amanda: "Is it to be mine for keeps?"
7. **A Birthday Feast**: Eva: "If I live to be a hundred years old..." Adele wondered why none wished her happy birthday; friends hadn't forgotten.
8. **More Surprises**: Adele alone at home; friends hide in dark library ("Happy Birthday!"); bird's-eye-maple writing desk (from Giant Father) with rose blotters; Jolly Pirates' fern; Mother's watercolor of the log cabin; Bob rings dinner bell; Kate's cake ("For my little Colleen, from Kate"); fortunes: Dick Jensen straw (farmer), Doris thimble, Jack silver dime, Rosamond wedding ring ("first bride").
9. **Mother Goose Play-House**: Sunday; Gertrude joins Adele at orphanage; 20 children ages 5-8, "good afternoon, Miss Adele." Mrs. Friend's sunny gardener's cottage. Betty's Mother Goose box from South (papa, architect). Bob "Good day to yez," cart; fudge bribe; Doris's bargain; Jack pries box; four Mother Goose cloths; Adele promises fudge party. Children: "Thank you, Miss Betty."
10. **Preparing for Examinations**: June; Uncle George's $100 check; bargain: pony if Betty passes spelling/grammar perfect; "courage and fearlessness" talk; Mrs. Burd objects; Betty studies ("i-e" words); Mr. Dickerson's oral exam averted (called away; Bob's message); Betty passes perfect grammar & spelling; excused from arithmetic (tutored summer). Pony Star. Melissy, colored maid; cold lemonade and nut-cookies on porch.
11. **Vacation Days**: Adele asks mother to invite Eva for two days; Mrs. Friend consents; Eva at Adele's house; wild-rose room; Japanese blue dragon bowl from Uncle Dixon (girl Wistaria); Jack: "Vanity! Vanity!"; Jolly Pirates want fudge.
12. **The Fudge Party**: Giant Father; Jack's chocolate purchase; phone invitations; Doris through hedge; Rosie late, "saw a ghost" (white tree trunk at cross-roads, burned home, Mr. Wiggin whitewashed it); Jolly Pirates' black hoods, "Fifteen men on a dead man's chest"; Lawrence Collins.
13. **The Two Dryads**: Adele and Eva climb Lookout Hill at dawn; names Dryad Oakleaf and Dryad Fern; artist Madge Peterson paints gnarled oak; invited to Little Bear Inn; telephone to Mrs. Doring (permission); Everett's capsized sailboat near Pine Island; Eva's "orphan" remark; Adele: "my mother says... it's what we are that counts."
14. **Pine Island**: Everett rows; Ching Ling's boxes: four fried chickens, lettuce sandwiches, olives, chocolate cake; Everett "I did not say a crumb."
15. **An Exciting Adventure**: Adele and Everett explore; man in bear skin digs iron box of gold; gunfire; cave; pirate flag; the Jolly Pirates (Pirate the Terrible) playing Treasure Island (Ben Gunn, Hispaniola).
16. **More Mystery**: Eva sketches; Madge offers Art Institute lessons; fisherman's boat; Little Bear story told by Jock-era fisherman (lumber camp, Kid Henderson, pigs, bear steals, mother bear killed).
17. **The Little Bear**: Little Bear raised with Kid; "Fiddler Fritz" teaches Kid to read; uncle (Kid's mother's brother) arrives; Kid to city school; Little Bear dies of poison; Kid is Eric Brownley, 15, prepping for college.
18. **A Fish Supper**: trout cooked; Eric arrives on horse Lightning; Mr. Wainwright (Betty's uncle) gives ride to town; Madge illustrates Miss Kimberly's children's verse.
19. **A Trip to the City**: Madge's visit; Eva may attend Art Institute Saturdays; Amanda's birthday; Amanda invited; Bob and Jack drive car ("footman").
20. **Amanda Brown**: Madge's city house by park; mother's singing; singing master; Amanda begins voice lessons.
21. **The Ball Game**: North High vs. South High; Eric absent (Dorset sub); Eric arrives on horse; North High wins.
22. **The King's Highway**: Madge's letter ("Dear Dryad Oakleaf"); Gertrude attends Institute with Adele; Roberty-Bob (hunchback, kitten Muffin); Gertrude's composition "The King's Highway" (Alicia) read aloud.
23. **School-Days Again**: Miss Donovan returns; plan Granny Dorset surprise party; purple silk dress from Bee Hive account; committees (Adele & Gertrude find old people; Peggy & Rosie sew dress).
24. **The House by the Wood**: Granny Dorset (Cherry Lane); old Quigleys in poorhouse; Miss Grackle's cabin, broth; "first two human beings... in ten years."
25. **A Visit to the Poorhouse**: Mrs. Quigley's "silver lining" saying; Grandpa Dally's miser story (long lank man, gold pieces, sheriff found cabin empty); Miranda Grackle story; Miss Grackle agrees to house Quigleys in cottage.
26. **A Mystery Solved**: chipmunk knocks gold bag from chimney ledge; note: "wasn't come by honest"; $1,000 deposited in First National Bank of Sunnyside; Miss Grackle pays Quigleys for garden work; party moved to cottage.
27. **A Really, Truly Home**: party; Mr. Quigley "Land sakes alive, ma!"; Granny Dorset gets purple silk dress; Grandpa Dally's wolf story (fur cap, woman's cabin, shot); Quigleys offered home by Miss Grackle.
28. **The New Pupil**: Susetta Green; Doris reports Greens; Susie's party invitations; Doris refuses for all; Mrs. Green takes Eva as servant/companion.
29. **Eva Begins a New Life**: directors refuse to lose donor; Eva's uncle Dick Dearman's letters returned "Dry Creek, Arizona"; Amanda wears Eva's blue ring.
30. **Eva Humiliated**: black dress, cap, apron; mending; Mrs. Green refuses Adele's visit ("servants' friends go to the side-door"); Mrs. Doring offers to adopt Eva.
31. **Something Unexpected**: Adele sees Eva in livery; Richard Dearman arrives at orphanage; Adele leads him to Restwell; Mr. Green knows "Dick Dearman"; Mrs. Green's lies; Susetta: "I won't tell Eva any such thing, ma, because it's a lie."
32. **A Happy Meeting**: Eva and uncle reunite in library; Mrs. Doring invites them to stay; Adele invited to Arizona next vacation.
33. **Farewell to the Orphanage**: Amanda also invited to go West; Mrs. Friend consents; Jack drives to station; Adele: "living in a story-book." Final line: "If you are also interested... 'Adele Doring on a Ranch.'"

# BOOK 2: Adele Doring at Boarding-School (Grace May North, 1921; Gutenberg 62360)

## Cast
- **Carol Lorens**: 15, new Sunnysider from Chicago suburb; father lawyer (lost fortune); mother; brother **Peter** (law student); twins **David and Dorothy** (7). Carol's family moved to father's boyhood farmhouse on Lake Road.
- **Mr. Dartmoor**: wealthy client; "ogre" (kind, shaggy gray eyebrows, blue eyes); granddaughter **Evelyn Dartmoor** (portrait with collie; boarding-school near Buffalo; mother died).
- **Madame Deriby**: Linden Hall matron (tall, silvery hair).
- **Linden Hall Seminary**: near Buffalo; ~40–48 pupils; Apple-Blossom Alley (corridor of creamy walls with apple-blossom border).
- **Gladys Merle Jones**: Chicago "Beef King" daughter; clique: **Anita Ryan** (echoes Gladys), **Janet Nagel** (later defects), **Jenny Clark**.
- **Patrick O'Neil** (groundskeeper, bus driver), **Billie/Bill** (stable boy), **Marie** (maid), **Miss Sharpleigh** (teacher), **Miss Merritt** (young teacher), **Mr. Haley** (riding-master), **Miss Berry** (kindergarten), **Miss Perring** (uniform maker), **Mr. O'Rourke** (farmer), **Miss Fenton** (Art Institute teacher, book 1 refs).
- **Gertrude Willis**: joins later as teacher of little ones in exchange for tuition.
- **Arthur Ellsworth** (18, lad of Elmhurst); **Aunt Louise (Miss Ellsworth)**; **Alise Alderly** (6, orphan, granddaughter of old Mr. Ellsworth; statue of her mother); **Mr. Diggitt** (gardener), **Mrs. Diggitt** (lodge).
- **Katrina Mason**: spoiled new pupil, tamed by Carol.
- **Matilda "Starr" Perkins**: Dakota prairie girl, 15; brothers **Cedric** (oldest) and **Basil**; dog **Shep**; mother Margaret Inslay (English), Bishop Wesley sent her; later revealed as niece of Mr. Barrington.
- **Geraldine Barrington**: haughty English roommate ("Lady Stuckup"), of Barrington Manor; father Mr. Barrington.
- **Peggy's fake ghost story**: Nina Best in cupola.
- **Marie Le Clerc**: wins French essay medal.
- **Donald Burnley**: Adele's "particular" friend (Adele's future Arizona cattleman).
- **Eva Dearman** (returns with Madge and Everett); **Madge Petersen** (chaperone for camp); **Everett Petersen**.
- Jolly Pirates: Jack, Bob Angel, Dick Jensen, Lawrence Collins, Arthur, Donald Burnley.

## Chapters
1. **A New Sunnysider**: Carol meets Sunnysiders at crossing; Gertrude introduces; Carol placed at Dorchester High (too advanced for Sunnyside school).
2. **The Ogre**: Carol's mother: boarding school for music/drawing; Carol delivers Mr. Dartmoor's legal papers; Mr. Dartmoor gives portrait-viewing; Evelyn lonely; Carol wishes to be with mother. Dorothy's "cloud with a silver lining."
3. **Two Surprises**: Evelyn's letter: "Dearest Granddad... Madame Deriby insists that I have a roommate." Mr. Dartmoor visits Lorens, offers Carol companion place at Linden Hall (Dorothy offers to help mother). Carol tells club. Sunny Seven: Miss Donovan's mother ill, Mr. Dickerson, Dorchester plan; Carol leaves; Adele: "Queer things happen!"
4. **New Faces and New Places**: train to Buffalo; Evelyn meets Carol at Linden station; school bus; Linden Hall elm drive; "Even Chinese if I had to!"
5. **A Letter from Carol**: letter to Sunnysiders (Madame Deriby "tall and stately"); Miss Donovan's mother; Dickerson; Adele's bones prophecy; Betty's uncle; five to Linden.
6. **Betty's Uncle George**: Betty stays home; Uncle George will pay tuition ("Betty Bobbets"). Madame Deriby's letter: "room for eight more girls... four double rooms"; bus meets train Saturday at four. Gertrude's regret.
7. **The Departure for Boarding-School**: Uncle Danny (deaf); boys Jack, Bob; Dick Jensen's candy boxes (Jensen candy shop, Jolly Pirates' gift); train departs.
8. **Apple-Blossom Alley**: Carol's letter from Adele; six arrive Saturday at four; Evelyn & Carol move to west wing; Adele-Betty room; Rosie-Bertha; Peggy-Doris "Inseparables"; corridor named "Apple-Blossom Alley"; Evelyn: Gladys Merle snobbery.
9. **Gladys Merle's Clique**: secret meeting; Anita writes letter to aunt; slip out gate at night; Patrick and Billie; Billie's "Huh! Nothin' but girls."
10. **The Downfall of Gladys Merle**: Miss Sharpleigh opens mail; Aunt Laura's letter (Carol's father a "poor lawyer," companion for Dartmoor granddaughter); Janet defends Carol; Janet defects; Gladys snubs Adele, Adele refuses to be cultivated.
11. **True Nobility**: Gladys's father Mr. Jones (red-faced, uneducated rancher) visits; Gladys hides; Carol's visit; great-grandfather Lorens refused royal title; "The Making of Royalty"; Gladys reconciles, visits father.
12. **A Wish Fulfilled**: pupils interviewed by Madame Deriby; Miss Berry leaves for brother; Gertrude hired to teach kindergarten; Adele's wish fulfilled (Gertrude coming); Gertrude to arrive Saturday.
13. **The New Teacher**: Mr. Willis phones; Gertrude's train stuck on siding; Patrick rescues; Gertrude "Oh, girls..."
14. **Orphan Alise**: Gertrude's youngest class (ages 5-7); Alise (6, golden hair, wistful): "Miss Gertrude, will you please let me love you?"; Elmhurst statue resembles Alise; name chiseled "Alise... El..."
15. **The Grandfather of Alise**: A. R. Ellsworth's trunks; Gertrude and Adele ride to Elmhurst; Arthur (18) and Aunt Louise; Alise Alderly; Louise's sister's baby; "Arthur, I am convinced..."
16. **Taming Katrina**: Madame Deriby asks girls; Carol's "loving kindness" approach; Katrina invited to rehearsal; Irish brogue role Norah; Katrina's goodies.
17. **An Unexpected Spread**: five o'clock visit; Katrina's welcome; Carol's introductions ("Adele Doring, a maiden fair..."); play read-through; feast hidden behind screens; Katrina apologizes; "taming complete."
18. **A Thanksgiving Dinner Party**: Ellsworth invitation (Louise Ellsworth), two o'clock Thanksgiving; chrysanthemums; "At the hour of three / A surprise there will be!"; Bob and Jack as "Russians" with Donald Burnley; Mr. Mellowisky; Arthur knew Jack and Bob from Dorchester; Betty: Arthur likes Gertrude.
19. **Just Skipping Along**: snow; Ellsworth sleigh-ride party at Elmhurst (Alise's birthday); Carol's Norah wins play praise; midwinter exams; Christmas; Jolly Pirates meet train; Adele's French essay contest (Marie Le Clerc wins; Adele second); Gladys's theater party in Buffalo; March: new pupil.
20. **The Old-Fashioned Pupil**: Peggy describes Matilda (plaid shawl, beaver cap, mittens); Gertrude brings Matilda Perkins; Bishop Wesley's protégée; Matilda assigned to Geraldine's room; Gertrude says: "The only creed of which we have need is the art of being kind."
21. **The Prairie Home**: Matilda's story (prairie, blizzard, Basil and Cedric rescue Bishop); Adele gives Matilda uniform; renames her "Starr" (double-r).
22. **Lady Stuckup**: Geraldine tries to leave; Matilda's diary; Peggy's ghost tale in cupola; Geraldine's sprained ankle; trailing arbutus; Matilda helps her; Mr. O'Rourke's wagon.
23. **A Dream That Came True**: Geraldine apologizes; Mr. Barrington's sister Margaret Inslay (Matilda's mother); Dakota; Adele invites Starr to visit.
24. **The C. E. P.**: closing-exercises party (C.E.P.); Gertrude's 16th birthday; Adele's secret; Donald Burnley (D.B.).
25. **A String of Pearls**: Uncle Pierson's $20 for Gertrude (she bought lilac silk for mother's convention dress); Evelyn treasurer; Betty's pink muslin dress altered by Adele (square neck, lace ruffles, pink fringed sash).
26. **Romancing**: Adele's Arizona cattleman wish; postman brigade: Eva coming, Amanda's baby daughter; Jack's letter: summer camping on uncle Jack and Aunt Dahlia's island in St. Lawrence River, August.
27. **Old Friends Arrive**: Madge invited as chaperone ("Lady of the Cabin"); Everett; Eva arrives; train on time; Arthur takes Everett home; Jolly Pirates to arrive.
28. **The Closing Party**: Rosie's pink rose; Starr's silver star circlet (Geraldine's gift); Hawaiian musicians; Madame Deriby and Madge; surprise for Gertrude: circle of girls sings "Happy birthday to our Gertrude"; Betty presents string of "friendship pearls."
29. **A Bud of a Romance**: orchard with Chinese lanterns; Arthur asks Gertrude to think of love; Gertrude: "I will gladly become your aunt's niece... but until then, I would rather not accept help."
30. **Farewell, Linden Hall**: Starr: "I want to take every one of you to my wonderful prairie home"; Adele's speech to Madame Deriby; "Farewell, Dear Linden Hall" song; Arthur drives tally-ho; last lines: Adele: "Sunnysiders, here endeth another chapter, and the next will be——" Betty finishes: "Adele Doring out camping!"
